name: Clontarf

attributes.attribute: site of Brian Bórama's 1014 victory over the Danes

text: Clontarf is a mythological location on the shore of Dublin Bay. The Irish name cluain tarbh means bull meadow. There Brian Bórama broke the power of the Danes on Good Friday of 1014. The clash became a landmark of Irish memory, retold in story and verse across the centuries. Clontarf now forms a northern suburb of the Dublin conurbation.

okr.objective: Clontarf is the Good Friday 1014 battlefield where Brian Bórama broke the Danes.
key_results: The place-name cluain tarbh means bull meadow in Irish.
Brian Bórama defeated Danish forces there on Good Friday 1014.
The battle took deep root in Irish memory, and the site is today a northern suburb of Dublin.
okr.evidence: MacKillop, Dictionary of Celtic Mythology, s.v. Clontarf
